inspection_summary: Verified the frozen SHA-256 and Python str.splitlines() count of 1,943, then inspected every normalized line. The article is mathematically coherent despite formula-layout risk: it compares a Ratios-Conjecture prediction for quadratic-Dirichlet one-level density with an unconditional explicit-formula calculation, isolates support-dependent lower-order terms, and supplies the character-sum, counting, partial-summation, and Poisson-error mechanisms needed for the comparison.

accepted_units.why_material: The source separates two research directions—larger Fourier support and lower-order terms—and explains that universal leading behavior can hide family arithmetic. It also records the Ratios recipe of keeping and completing diagonal pieces and differentiating uniformly, together with its strategic value in suggesting how apparently different answers should be grouped.

accepted_units.title: The explicit formula converts a zero statistic into conductor and prime-power terms
accepted_units.why_material: States the family explicit formula and explains the comparison architecture: conductor and Gamma terms already match, quadraticity reduces prime powers to the behaviors of χ_d(p) and χ_d(p)^2, and the Ratios answer suggests non-obvious simplifications of those number-theory sums.

accepted_units.title: Isolating the unmatched Ratios term and forecasting two odd-sum error routes
accepted_units.why_material: Decomposes the Ratios-side expression into already matched pieces and a hardest residual integral R(g;X), identifies its pole contribution, and relates its RH-dependent support error to the weaker Jutila route and the stronger Poisson route on the number-theory side.

accepted_units.title: Fourier support annihilates the asymptotic tail and exposes finite-size corrections
accepted_units.why_material: Gives a lower-cost alternative mechanism: truncate by Schwartz decay, Taylor-expand fixedly many factors, and interpret the resulting integrals as Fourier transforms of derivatives evaluated outside support. It also explains why the first 1/log X term matters for finite matrix-size modeling.
accepted_units.context_note: A methodological remark rather than the sharp contour proof; it clarifies what compact support is doing structurally.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The three-step mechanism is prose-recoverable; the intermediate expansion at lines 382–391 should be scan-checked if used literally.

accepted_units.title: Contour shifting separates the symmetry residue from zeta-zero errors
accepted_units.why_material: Simplifies the arithmetic factor to a zeta ratio, supplies complex-shift decay and Gamma-ratio controls, and shifts the residual integral across the pole giving −g(0)/2 and the poles induced by zeta zeros. The support of the Fourier transform then determines the power saving, while the shifted contour is negligible.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the sharp proof of the residual Ratios term under RH and explicitly distinguishes the universal residue from the zero-driven error.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The logical contour structure is readable; pole locations, Gamma/zeta ratios, and powers of X are formula-sensitive and need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Subtracting the zeta pole regularizes an integral on the contour
accepted_units.why_material: Shows an alternate local maneuver for a pole lying on the line of integration: split zeta into its principal part and a regular remainder, use evenness to symmetrize the principal-value integral, and recover the sine-kernel contribution −g(0)/2.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides a reusable regularization viewpoint complementary to the full contour shift.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The pole-subtraction argument is prose-recoverable; signs and Fourier normalization in the displayed integral should be checked against the scan.
